content: Difficulty sleeping may occur as a side effect of this medication. It is important to understand that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the potential benefits to your health outweigh the risks of side effects. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare, but they can occur. This document does not provide a complete list of possible side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Similarly, if you are in Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Precautions: Before starting ledipasvir/sofosbuvir, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to either of these drugs or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. If you have diabetes, be aware that hepatitis C treatment may lower your blood sugar levels, increasing the risk of hypoglycemia. Your doctor may need to adjust your diabetes treatment plan accordingly. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when absolutely necessary. Discuss the potential risks and benefits with your doctor. The combination of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir with ribavirin must not be used during pregnancy by either the pregnant woman or her male partner, as it may harm the unborn baby. Reliable forms of birth control must be used whenever at least one sexual partner is taking these medications together. Female patients should continue using birth control for nine months after stopping treatment, while male patients should continue for six months after stopping treatment. It is not known whether this medication passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may slow the removal of other drugs from your body, potentially affecting how they work. Conversely, other medications may affect the removal of ledipasvir/sofosbuvir from your body, which could impact its effectiveness. Examples of such medications include apalutamide and rifamycins (e.g., rifampin, rifabutin). Overdose: In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory Tests: Before starting this medication, while using it, and after completing treatment, laboratory tests (such as liver function tests and tests for hepatitis B and C) should be conducted. If you are using this medication with ribavirin, it is recommended that female patients or female partners of male patients take a pregnancy test before starting treatment. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is less than six hours before your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Keep the tablets in their original container. For the pellet form, do not open the packets until you are ready to use the medication. Do not store this medication in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
